Q: When creating a new 'ColorSpec' in the Material Color Utilities library, do I also need to modify the 'variants.ts' file as well? A:

Hey i believe you should try creating a custom color spec without touching your variant.ts file but just make sure to use the existing variant values even if you create new ones. so in short words, you dont need to necessarily modify other code files just make sure that you are using the values you already have 👍

Q: Merge / convert multiple PDF files into one PDF A:

I used qpdf from the terminal, and it works for me on Windows (MobaXterm) and Linux, for example the command for join A.pdf with B.pdf at new file C.pdf is:

qpdf --empty --pages oficios/A.pdf  informes/B.pdf -- salida/C.PDF

If you need more documentation, see MobaXterm.

Q: Change the encoding of a file in Visual Studio Code A:

So here's how to do that:

In the bottom bar of VSCode, you'll see the label UTF-8. Click it. A popup opens. Click Save with encoding. (You can also reach this with the Command Palette, Ctrl+Shift+P and type Change file encoding > Save with encoding. You can now pick a new encoding for that file, for example, "UTF-8 with BOM" (aka utf8bom).

Alternatively, you can change the setting globally in Workspace/User settings using the setting "files.encoding": "utf8". If using the graphical settings page in VSCode, simply search for encoding. Do note however that this only applies to newly created files.

Q: Parsing escaped quotes in a string A:

Doc for QuotedString

esc_quote - special quote sequence to re_escape an embedded quote string 
            (such as SQL’s "" to re_escape an embedded ") (default= None)

So you may use esc_quote='\\"' instead of esc_char='\\'

Minimal working code with other examples - like mentioned SQL’s ""

import pyparsing as pp

# ----- original

print("\n----- original: esc_char:", "\\", "\n")

string_literal = pp.QuotedString('"', esc_char="\\", convert_whitespace_escapes=False)

s = r'" embedded quote \" embedded expression \(1+2)  "'
print(f"s: >{s}<")

r = string_literal.parse_string(s)[0]
print(f"r: >{r}<")

# -----

print("\n----- esc_quote:", '\\"', "\n")

string_literal = pp.QuotedString('"', esc_quote='\\"', convert_whitespace_escapes=False)

s = r'" embedded quote \" embedded expression \(1+2)  "'
print(f"s: >{s}<")

r = string_literal.parse_string(s)[0]
print(f"r: >{r}<")

# -----

print("\n----- esc_quote:", '""', "\n")

string_literal = pp.QuotedString('"', esc_quote='""', convert_whitespace_escapes=False)

s = r'" embedded quote "" embedded expression \(1+2)  "'
print(f"s: >{s}<")

r = string_literal.parse_string(s)[0]
print(f"r: >{r}<")

# -----

print("\n----- esc_quote:", '{"}', "\n")

string_literal = pp.QuotedString('"', esc_quote='{"}', convert_whitespace_escapes=False)

s = r'" embedded quote {"} embedded expression \(1+2)  "'
print(f"s: >{s}<")

r = string_literal.parse_string(s)[0]
print(f"r: >{r}<")

# -----

print("\n----- esc_quote:", "'\"'", "\n")

string_literal = pp.QuotedString(
    '"', esc_quote="'\"'", convert_whitespace_escapes=False
)

s = '" embedded quote \'"\' embedded expression \\(1+2)  "'
print(f"s: >{s}<")

r = string_literal.parse_string(s)[0]
print(f"r: >{r}<")

Result:

----- original: esc_char: \

s: >" embedded quote \" embedded expression \(1+2)  "<
r: > embedded quote " embedded expression (1+2)  <

----- esc_quote: \"

s: >" embedded quote \" embedded expression \(1+2)  "<
r: > embedded quote " embedded expression \(1+2)  <

----- esc_quote: ""

s: >" embedded quote "" embedded expression \(1+2)  "<
r: > embedded quote " embedded expression \(1+2)  <

----- esc_quote: {"}

s: >" embedded quote {"} embedded expression \(1+2)  "<
r: > embedded quote " embedded expression \(1+2)  <

----- esc_quote: '"'

s: >" embedded quote '"' embedded expression \(1+2)  "<
r: > embedded quote " embedded expression \(1+2)  <
